Seda Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Seda's Jewish community grew to become the largest in the region within a few decades of its likely 17th-century founding, peaking at 1,729 people in 1847. About 40 families maintained agricultural farms on roughly 100 hectares in a nearby settlement neighbors called Zydu Dvaras, the 'Jewish Farm.' On June 23, 1941, the day after the German invasion, all of Seda's Jews were herded into that very farm and held without food or water for days; on July 3, armed Lithuanians took the men out and murdered them near this cemetery, and on August 9, women and children were taken to the Jewish cemetery in Mažeikiai, documented elsewhere in this collection, and murdered alongside Jews from surrounding towns. This cemetery, dating to the end of the 17th century, was almost destroyed during the Soviet period — locals used its tombstones to build house foundations and the Varduva dam, and a nearby resident later dug a pond on its grounds.
